summary_markdown:
**Company and People**

*   **Company:** Oakline Property Group
    *   **What it does:** Manages maintenance for 340 units across six buildings.
*   **People:**
    *   **Speaker (Interviewer):** Operations Manager at Oakline Property Group.
    *   **Carlos:** Maintenance Coordinator.
    *   **Linda Park:** Owner of the management company.

**Workflow Steps**

| Step | Who | Tool |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resident submits request via Appfolio, emails leasing office, or texts Carlos | Residents | Appfolio, Email, Text |
| Carlos checks portal, email, and text; decides between in-house technician or outside vendor | Carlos | Appfolio, Gmail, Personal Cell Phone |
| Carlos assigns work order to technician/vendor from vendor list | Carlos | Excel Spreadsheet (Vendor List) |
| Vendor is contacted (call/text); resident notified of arrival time | Carlos/Leasing Office | Phone/Text |
| Vendor performs repair; invoice sent (sometimes with photos) | Vendor | - |
| Carlos closes work order in Appfolio and attaches invoice | Carlos | Appfolio |

**Volumes and Timing**

*   340 units managed across six buildings.
*   ~90 work orders per month.
*   ~15 emergency requests per month.
*   ~30 status calls per week.
*   Status call duration: 5–10 minutes each.
*   Work order closure time: Average 9 days.
*   Vendor show-up failure rate: 1 out of every 8 appointments.
*   Unmatched invoices frequency: 2–3 times per month.
*   Shared spreadsheet usage duration: ~3 weeks.

**Tools and Systems**

*   Appfolio (Resident portal, work orders)
*   Gmail
*   Personal Cell Phone
*   Excel Spreadsheet (Vendor List)
*   Whiteboard (in Carlos's office)
*   QuickBooks (for paying vendor invoices)

**Pain Points**

| Pain | Cost or impact |
| --- | --- |
| Vendors do not show up or arrive late; no record kept in system. | Residents call upset; no one knows what happened because info was only in Carlos's texts. |
| High volume of status calls to leasing team. | ~30 calls per week; 5–10 minutes each to find Carlos and ask for updates. |
| Open work orders take too long to close (avg 9 days). | Bad reviews from residents who feel ignored; Owner reports show unfinished work incorrectly. |
| After-hours emergency requests often lack proper documentation. | Invoices cannot be matched to units; bookkeeper must email Carlos to dig through texts. |
| Lack of visibility when Carlos is on vacation. | No vendor phone numbers available; unknown job schedules; residents told someone would come but nobody did. |

**Desired Outcome and Measure**

*   **Outcome:** Every request enters Appfolio within an hour regardless of source; every resident receives updates when a vendor is scheduled and when work is done without relying on Carlos's memory.
*   **Measure:** Reduce status calls to the leasing office by half (from 30/week); reduce average days to close a work order (currently 9).

**Decision Makers**

*   **Sign-off:** Operations Manager and Linda Park (Owner of management company).
*   **Required involvement:** Carlos (Maintenance Coordinator) must be present to know where issues are occurring.

**Next Steps**

| Owner | Action | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Speaker | Export one month of work orders from Appfolio with names removed | Monday |
| Speaker | Conduct a short call with Linda Park and Carlos | Next week |
| Speaker | Present proposal for one-lane request intake and resident status updates as a pilot on one building, one agent | Next week |
